mainTopic: The source and minimum amount for deliberate מעילה, three readings of the ברייתא's contrast, and why חמץ separated on פסח cannot become תרומה (״לו ולא לאורו״)
overview: This עמוד continues a discussion from the previous עמוד, where רב חייא בר אבין explained a ברייתא according to אבא שאול, who measures מעילה by שוה פרוטה. The גמרא identifies the view that deliberate מעילה is punished by death as רבי's view. רבי אבהו explains that רבי learns it from תרומה through the shared word חטא. That link seems to require a כזית for מעילה, but רב פפא answers that רבי may measure תרומה itself by שוה פרוטה, like אבא שאול. The גמרא then concludes that רב פפא retracted a contrary statement of his own. Next, מר בריה דרבנא and רב נחמן בר יצחק each read the ברייתא's contrast differently: מעילה is stricter because one is liable even without intent for that object, or even as a מתעסק. The גמרא then turns to a ruling about תרומה and חמץ. חמץ separated as תרומה on פסח does not become holy, based on ״תתן לו ולא לאורו״. This is limited to grain that never had a שעת הכושר, and רב נחמן בר יצחק affirms that חמץ which leavened after being cut does become תרומה. The עמוד ends as a report from רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע begins; it continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Identifying the view that intentional misuse of sacred property is punished by death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the opinion 'intentional מעילה is punished by death' belongs to רבי, and it brings a ברייתא to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view that one who intentionally misuses sacred property is punished with death is the view of רבי. As a ברייתא teaches: if someone intentionally misused sacred property, רבי says he is punished with death at the hands of Heaven, and the חכמים say he has only violated a regular prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question earlier: who holds that intentional מעילה carries מיתה בידי שמים? It quotes a ברייתא showing that this is רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pinning the view on רבי matters for the argument that follows. Once we know it is רבי's view, the גמרא can look at where רבי learns it from. That source will turn out to affect the question of minimum amounts.

keyTerms.meaning: Did it on purpose (intentionally)
Improper use of הקדש (sacred property)
Death, here מיתה בידי שמים (death at the hands of Heaven)
A warning, meaning a regular לאו (prohibition) without a death penalty

steps.confusionAlert: The 'מיתה' here is not a court execution. It means מיתה בידי שמים, a death penalty that comes from Heaven.

phrases.english: One who intentionally misuses sacred property is liable to death —
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting this line of the ברייתא again, to figure out who said it.

phrases.english: it is the view of Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi),
as it was taught: one who intentionally misused sacred property,
Rabbi says: he is liable to death (at the hands of Heaven),
and the Sages say: he has violated a warning (a regular prohibition).
phrases.notes: According to the חכמים he gets מלקות, not מיתה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵזִיד בִּמְעִילָה בְּמִיתָה — רַבִּי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous דף about who holds that intentional מעילה is punished by death.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the author of the view that intentional מעילה is punished by death?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי, as shown by an explicit ברייתא where he argues with the חכמים.

steps.title: Asking for רבי's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי holds that intentional מעילה is punished by death.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for רבי's view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי gets his ruling from. This question sets up the next step, where רבי אבהו gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not openly state a death penalty for מעילה, so רבי must be learning it from somewhere. Knowing the exact source will show what else carries over from that source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason / source?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view just attributed to רבי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי's ruling that intentional מעילה is punished by death.

steps.title: רבי learns it from the word חטא in the laws of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that רבי uses a גזירה שוה: the word חטא appears both by מעילה and by תרומה. Since eating תרומה improperly carries death, so does מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: רבי learns it from the word 'sin' that appears in both places, connecting מעילה to תרומה. Just as תרומה is punished with death, so too מעילה is punished with death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives רבי's source: a word-link (גזירה שוה) between מעילה and תרומה, based on the shared word חטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about מעילה says 'וחטאה בשגגה' (ויקרא ה:טו), and the verse about תרומה says 'ולא ישאו עליו חטא ומתו בו' (ויקרא כב:ט). Because both use the word חטא, the death penalty in תרומה carries over to מעילה. This link is the key to the next step, since a גזירה שוה can carry other details along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (derives), here by a גזירה שוה
Sin, the word shared by both verses
The portion of produce given to a כהן, forbidden to a זר (non-כהן)
Just as... so too..., the comparison formula

steps.whyThisMatters: Once מעילה is tied to תרומה, the גמרא can ask whether the minimum amount for תרומה also carries over to מעילה. That question drives the rest of this passage.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
He derives 'sin' 'sin' from terumah.
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word appears in both contexts.

phrases.english: Just as terumah is punished with death —
so too misuse of sacred property is punished with death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of רבי's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of the word חטא, linking מעילה to תרומה, which carries the death penalty.

steps.title: So מעילה should need a כזית, just like תרומה
steps.stepSummary: From the same link, the גמרא argues that מעילה should need a כזית like תרומה. That would mean the ברייתא cannot follow אבא שאול, who uses שוה פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from this same comparison: just as תרומה requires a כזית, so too מעילה should require a כזית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stretches the תרומה-מעילה link to the minimum amount. If מעילה is like תרומה, it should need a כזית, and this undercuts רב חייא בר אבין's claim that the ברייתא follows אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that תרומה is measured by a כזית, as the חכמים hold. If רבי copies the rules of תרומה over to מעילה, then according to רבי מעילה is measured by a כזית, not by שוה פרוטה. So רבי, the author of the ברייתא, would not agree with אבא שאול, and רב חייא בר אבין's explanation falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And from it (from the same comparison, we learn more)
An olive-bulk, the standard minimum amount for eating

steps.confusionAlert: The exclamation mark shows that this is a challenge, not a new ruling. The גמרא is pointing out an uncomfortable result for the earlier explanation of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And from it (the same comparison):
just as terumah is measured by an olive-bulk,
so too misuse of sacred property is measured by an olive-bulk!
phrases.notes: So the ברייתא cannot follow אבא שאול, who uses a שוה פרוטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִינַּהּ: מָה תְּרוּמָה בִּכְזַיִת אַף מְעִילָה בִּכְזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי אבהו's גזירה שוה to the minimum amount, which produces a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חייא בר אבין's explanation that the ברייתא follows אבא שאול (שוה פרוטה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא is רבי's. רבי links מעילה to תרומה, and תרומה needs a כזית, so according to רבי מעילה needs a כזית. That contradicts אבא שאול.

steps.title: רב פפא: perhaps רבי holds like אבא שאול about תרומה too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the challenge. Who says רבי agrees with the חכמים that תרומה needs a כזית? Perhaps he holds like אבא שאול that תרומה is measured by שוה פרוטה even without a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא strongly objected: How do you know that רבי agrees with the חכמים? Perhaps he agrees with אבא שאול, who said that if it has the value of a פרוטה, he is liable, even though it is less than a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends רב חייא בר אבין by questioning the hidden assumption of the challenge. The challenge assumed that רבי measures תרומה by a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if רבי measures תרומה by a כזית. If רבי holds like אבא שאול that תרומה is measured by שוה פרוטה, then the גזירה שוה moves שוה פרוטה over to מעילה, not a כזית. So the ברייתא can still follow אבא שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it
From where (do you know)?
Perhaps
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin value
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: רבי learns that intentional מעילה carries death from תרומה (חטא-חטא). Whether that link brings along a כזית or a שוה פרוטה depends on how רבי measures תרומה. רב פפא says רבי may hold like אבא שאול (שוה פרוטה), which keeps רב חייא בר אבין's explanation alive.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not arguing about מעילה directly. He changes the starting point, which is how רבי measures תרומה. Whatever is true for תרומה automatically carries over to מעילה.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa strongly objects to it:
From where do you know that Rabbi holds like the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The Rabbis hold that תרומה is measured by a כזית.

phrases.english: Perhaps he holds like Abba Shaul,
who said: if it contains the value of a peruta —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית בַּהּ כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: he is liable, even though it does not contain an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: מִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי כְּרַבָּנַן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 4 by challenging its hidden assumption about how רבי measures תרומה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי's ברייתא cannot follow אבא שאול.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that רבי holds like the חכמים that תרומה needs a כזית. He may instead hold like אבא שאול (שוה פרוטה), and then the גזירה שוה gives מעילה a שוה פרוטה measure.

steps.title: רב פפא himself said אבא שאול requires two conditions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's answer. He himself elsewhere said that אבא שאול requires both a כזית and a שוה פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it רב פפא himself who said that אבא שאול requires two things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer רב פפא just gave. That answer contradicts something רב פפא said elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רב פפא said that according to אבא שאול, a שוה פרוטה is enough even without a כזית. But רב פפא is on record saying that אבא שאול requires both, a כזית and a שוה פרוטה. So רב פפא seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: He requires two (conditions)
But isn't it so that... (opens a contradiction)

phrases.english: But isn't it Rav Pappa who said
that Abba Shaul requires two (an olive-bulk and a peruta's worth)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of step 5 by pointing to a contradictory statement from the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that אבא שאול holds a שוה פרוטה suffices without a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: רב פפא elsewhere says אבא שאול requires both a כזית and a שוה פרוטה.

steps.title: Conclusion: רב פפא changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רב פפא retracted one of his two statements about אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that he retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction from step 6. It concludes that רב פפא changed his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two statements truly cannot both stand, so the גמרא does not try to reconcile them. It says רב פפא retracted his view that אבא שאול needs two conditions. This leaves his answer in step 5 intact.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, learn from this
He retracted (changed his mind)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rejection of רב פפא. The answer from step 5 survives, and his earlier statement is the one considered withdrawn.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this: he retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the contradictory statements is withdrawn
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא contradicts himself, so his answer in step 5 falls.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב פפא retracted, so his step 5 answer (רבי follows אבא שאול's שוה פרוטה) stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge to the ברייתא is answered. רבי can hold like אבא שאול that a שוה פרוטה is the measure, and רב פפא is understood to have retracted his other statement.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבנא: in מעילה even acting on the wrong object counts
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבנא explains the ברייתא's contrast differently. In other מצוות, someone who acted without proper intent is exempt. In מעילה, he is liable even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבנא said: This is what the ברייתא means. No! You may say that in other מצוות, acting without intent is not treated like acting with intent. For example, if someone meant to cut something detached and instead cut something attached, he is exempt. But will you say the same about מעילה? There, if someone meant to warm himself with ordinary wool and warmed himself with wool of an עולה, he has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא that contrasted מעילה with other מצוות. It gives a new explanation that does not need רבי's view about a death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanation of this ברייתא (discussed in steps 1–7) read the contrast as being about the death penalty for deliberate מעילה, which is רבי's view. מר בריה דרבנא instead reads it as a matter of intent. On שבת, cutting the wrong item by mistake exempts you, because you did not intend the forbidden act on that object. With מעילה, you are liable even if you meant to use permitted wool and used holy wool instead.

keyTerms.meaning: One who intends (the act on this object)
Detached from the ground (cutting it is permitted on שבת)
Attached to the ground (cutting it is a forbidden מלאכה)
Wool shearings of a burnt-offering (holy property)
He committed מעילה (misused holy property)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic idea: מעילה depends on the fact that holy property was used. It does not depend on what the person meant to do. That is why it is stricter than other איסורים.

phrases.english: Mar son of Rabbana said:
This is what it (the baraita) is saying: No!
If you said so regarding the other מצוות,
where [the Torah] did not make in them
one who does not intend like one who intends,
for if he intended to cut something detached
and he cut something attached, he is exempt;
will you say so regarding misuse of consecrated property,
where if he intended to warm himself with non-sacred shearings
and he warmed himself with shearings of a burnt-offering, he has misused?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבְנָא אָמַר הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי/רב פפא thread. It offers a different reading of the ברייתא that step 1 had attributed to רבי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's contrast refers to the death penalty for deliberate מעילה, which is רבי's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The contrast refers to intent. Other מצוות exempt one who acted on the wrong object, while מעילה does not.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: in מעילה even an unaware act counts
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a third reading of the ברייתא. In other מצוות, a מתעסק (someone who did not intend the act at all) is exempt. In מעילה, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: This is what the ברייתא means. No! You may say that in other מצוות, a person who acts unaware is not liable like someone who acts aware. For example, if someone meant to lift something detached and cut something attached, he is exempt. But will you say the same about מעילה? There, if someone reached into a vessel to take an object and smeared his hand with holy oil, he has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives yet another explanation of the same ברייתא. His explanation focuses on a person who did not mean to do the act at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בריה דרבנא's case involved someone who meant to cut, just not that item. רב נחמן בר יצחק's case involves someone who did not mean to cut at all, only to lift. He is a מתעסק. Even in this weaker kind of intent, מעילה still makes you liable, as when a hand reaching for an object gets smeared with holy oil.

keyTerms.meaning: One who acts unaware, without intending the act at all
To lift
He stretched out his hand
Holy (consecrated) oil

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In step 8, the person meant to CUT but cut the wrong thing (אין מתכוין). In step 9, he only meant to LIFT and did not mean to cut at all (מתעסק).
steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of the ברייתא's contrast. רב חייא בר אבין reads the stringency of מעילה as death for deliberate מעילה, which is רבי's view. מר בריה דרבנא reads it as liability even without intent for that object. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads it as liability even for a מתעסק.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
This is what it is saying: No!
If you said so regarding the other מצוות,
since one is not made liable in them
one acting unaware like one acting aware,
for if he intended to lift something detached
and he cut something attached, he is exempt;
will you say so regarding misuse of consecrated property,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם הוֹשִׁיט יָדוֹ לִכְלִי לִיטּוֹל חֵפֶץ
phrases.english: where if he stretched his hand into a vessel to take an object

phrases.aramaic: וְסָךְ יָדוֹ בְּשֶׁמֶן שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ — שֶׁמָּעַל.
phrases.english: and smeared his hand with consecrated oil, he has misused?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel alternative to step 8. It reads the same ברייתא with a stronger case of lacking intent (מתעסק).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The contrast concerns the death penalty for deliberate מעילה (רב חייא בר אבין's reading, based on רבי's view) or acting on the wrong object (מר בריה דרבנא).
steps.terutzMaskana: The contrast concerns a מתעסק. Other מצוות exempt him, but מעילה makes him liable.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: תרומה that became חמץ versus חמץ separated as תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier ברייתא about eating תרומה that is חמץ on פסח. It quotes a clarification: the dispute applies only to תרומה that became חמץ after being separated. Separating חמץ as תרומה on פסח does not make it holy, according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: When does this apply? When someone separated תרומה and it later became חמץ. But if someone separated חמץ as תרומה, everyone agrees it is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting a line from the earlier ברייתא. It is setting up a discussion of that line, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's dispute (about paying for eaten תרומה that is חמץ) is limited to a case where the תרומה was valid when separated and only later became חמץ. If the food was already חמץ during פסח when separated, it is worthless and forbidden. So the separation does not take effect at all, and everyone agrees on this.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (limits a ruling)
It became leavened (חמץ)
Everyone agrees
It is not holy (the תרומה status does not take effect)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that תרומה status needs an item the כהן can actually use. Since חמץ on פסח cannot be eaten, separating it as תרומה does not take effect. The next steps give the source.

phrases.english: The Master said:
In what case are these words said?
Where one separated teruma and it became leavened;
but if he separated leavened bread as teruma,
all agree it is not consecrated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the מעילה discussion and returns to analyze a further line of the earlier תרומה/חמץ ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies only to תרומה that became חמץ after separation. חמץ separated as תרומה on פסח is not holy, according to all.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that חמץ separated as תרומה on פסח does not become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule just stated: separating חמץ as תרומה on פסח does not make it holy. This is a setup line, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said everyone agrees on this rule, even those who allow benefit from חמץ on פסח. So the reason cannot simply be that חמץ is forbidden for benefit. The גמרא wants a פסוק that explains it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things known? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: Refers back to the rule from Step 10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule just quoted in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that חמץ separated on פסח cannot become תרומה.

steps.title: Give it to him, not to his fire
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק derives the rule from ״תתן לו״: תרומה must be usable by the כהן, not just burnable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The פסוק says, 'you shall give to him,' and not to his fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers from the פסוק ״תתן לו״. תרומה must be given 'to him,' meaning something the כהן can actually use. It cannot be something that is only good for burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if one may benefit from חמץ on פסח, it certainly cannot be eaten. The only use left is to burn it, so it would go 'to his fire.' Something like that cannot become תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall give to him (the כהן) — from the פסוק about ראשית
And not to his fire — not something fit only for burning

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates the principle that תרומה must be something the כהן can use. It drives the rest of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
The verse states: 'You shall give to him'
— and not to his fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״תתן לו״ requires that תרומה be usable by the כהן. Since חמץ on פסח can only be burned, it cannot become תרומה.

steps.title: Objection from impure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע points out that impure תרומה is also only fit for burning, yet the משנה says it still counts as תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע objected: We do not separate תרומה from impure produce for pure produce, but if someone did so by mistake, his תרומה is valid תרומה. But why? Let us say: 'to him' and not to his fire!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenges the new principle using a משנה. Impure תרומה can only be burned, yet if it was separated by mistake, it still counts as תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה may not be eaten and must be burned. That is exactly the 'to his fire' situation. If ״לו ולא לאורו״ were a rule, this תרומה should not take effect either.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate תרומה
Ritually impure / ritually pure produce
By mistake, unintentionally

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, raised an objection:
One may not separate teruma from impure produce for pure produce,
but if he separated it unwittingly —
his teruma is valid teruma.
But why? Let us say:
'To him,' and not to his fire!
phrases.notes: Impure תרומה can only be burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation of ״לו ולא לאורו״ from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's principle that something fit only for burning cannot become תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Impure תרומה is fit only for burning, yet the משנה says it takes effect. This contradicts the principle.

steps.title: Impure produce once had a time of fitness
steps.stepSummary: Impure produce was once fit to be given, but this חמץ never was. That is why only the חמץ fails to become תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. There, it had a time of fitness. Here, it did not have a time of fitness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by contrasting the two cases. The impure produce was once pure and fit to give to a כהן. This חמץ never had such a moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לו ולא לאורו״ blocks only something that was never fit to give to the כהן. Since the impure produce once had a שעת הכושר, it can still become תרומה. The principle now applies only to items with no time of fitness at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult — introduces an answer
A time of fitness, when the item was fit for its purpose
There / here — contrasting two cases

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the impure produce is 'not really תרומה.' It is full תרומה, and only its use is limited to burning. The difference is only whether there was ever a שעת הכושר.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
there, it had a period of fitness,
phrases.notes: The impure produce was once pure.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא לֹא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: here, it did not have a period of fitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָתָם הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any item fit only for burning cannot become תרומה, so impure תרומה should not take effect either.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an item that never had a שעת הכושר is excluded by ״לו ולא לאורו״. Impure produce once had one, so it still becomes תרומה.

steps.title: When did the חמץ never have a time of fitness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the case where the חמץ never had a time of fitness. Answer: when it became חמץ while still attached to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the case where it never had a time of fitness, what is it like? For example, where it became חמץ while still attached to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exact case of חמץ never had a time of fitness. It answers that the grain became חמץ while still attached to the ground, before it could ever be separated as תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce cannot become תרומה while still attached to the ground. So if it became חמץ before it was cut, there was never a moment when it was fit to be given as תרומה. This narrows the rule to a very specific case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
It became חמץ (leavened)
Attached to the ground

phrases.english: And where it did not have a period of fitness,
what are the circumstances?
For example, where it became leavened while attached to the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְלֹא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case of 'no שעת הכושר' from Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of חמץ truly never had a time of fitness.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Grain that became חמץ while still attached to the ground.

steps.title: Would חמץ that leavened after cutting become holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, by this logic, חמץ that leavened after being cut would become תרומה even on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it became חמץ after it was detached — would it indeed become holy?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks רב נחמן בר יצחק about a surprising result of the last answer. If the grain became חמץ after it was cut, it once had a time of fitness, so would it become תרומה even if separated on פסח? The next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 sounded like no חמץ at all can become תרומה on פסח. The new limit would make the rule apply only to grain that leavened while attached, which is a rare case. The question presses whether this is really the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached, cut from the ground
Is it really so? — testing a surprising result
It became holy (takes effect as תרומה)

phrases.english: But if it became leavened after being detached —
would it indeed become consecrated?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אַחְמֵיץ בְּתָלוּשׁ הָכִי נָמֵי דְּקָדְשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a difficult result from the case defined in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The narrowing of the rule to grain that leavened while attached
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, חמץ that leavened after cutting would become תרומה on פסח. That seems to go against the plain sense of the rule in Step 10.

steps.title: Yes, and the בית המדרש rules this way
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק accepts the result: such חמץ does become holy. He adds that the חכמים agree and the בית המדרש rules like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. 'The matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the sentence by the word of the holy ones.' And so they rule in the study hall like me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק says yes: חמץ that leavened after being cut does become תרומה even if separated on פסח. He supports this by saying the חכמים agree and the בית המדרש rules like him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not avoid the surprising result. He accepts it fully. The פסוק from דניאל is used as a playful way to say the 'holy ones,' meaning the חכמים, have decided this. So the rule of Step 10 applies only to grain that leavened while attached.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Watchers (angels) — here applied to the חכמים
The study hall
Like me, in accordance with my view

steps.whatToRemember: ״תתן לו ולא לאורו״: something that was never fit to give the כהן cannot become תרומה. Impure produce and חמץ that leavened after cutting both had a שעת הכושר, so they do become תרומה. Only grain that leavened while attached is excluded.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
'The matter is by the decree of the watchers,'
'and the sentence by the word of the holy ones,'
and so they rule in the study hall in accordance with me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the result raised in Step 16 as the actual הלכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, חמץ that leavened after cutting does become תרומה, and the בית המדרש rules this way.

steps.title: Transition: when רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע came
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a report about what happened when רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע arrived. It continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא son of רב יהושע came,
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up what comes next. The גמרא is about to tell what רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said when he arrived, and the content continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ruling is given yet. The formula ״כי אתא״ usually brings a report from another place. Here it will likely add to the discussion that just ended.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came — introduces a report

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: When Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, came,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a report that follows the exchange in Steps 13–17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is a setup line for the next passage.
